action_summary: The write-authority rule refuses a destination that IS a source the action also named. It cannot see a destination that is a source file nobody named -- which is exactly what the binder produces when a sentence names a file and the row declares both output_path and source_root. Reproduced on main f4e6cdb, in the repository: run_adapter_locally('software.hardcore.kernel.orchestrate.v1', {'args': {'output_path': '…/u.py'}}) RAN and replaced 51 bytes of Python with 1,134 bytes of JSON report. Parsing was not enough to catch it -- the report compiles as a dict literal -- so the destination is now watched across the run: if a module became a non-module the original bytes go back and the call fails. 25 write tests, 18 door and formatter tests and the 28-sentence surface census all still pass.
blocker_lease_key: 2026-10-09-resource-bounded-bytes-v1::GENERAL_REUSABLE_PROBLEM_SOLVING_CAPABILITY_FRONTIER::`write_authority.violation` compares a destination against the source SLOTS that were bound. When no directory is in the sentence the source slot is empty, so a report bound onto the only stated path is invisible to the rule, and `compile()` accepts the report as Python.

AFTER: the same call raises OUTPUT_REPLACED_A_SOURCE_WITH_NON_SOURCE:/…/u.py:bytes=51->1134 and the file is byte-for-byte the original module again.
